transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Stop there. Speak softly. This fountain does not forgive noise.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am Salim, and I have come for my brother Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Keep those names inside your mouth, or the oil will swallow them. I see boys like you arrive here, but I never see them leave.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't care about that. I only care about finding him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You say that now. But this place eats your mind first. You will forget why you came before you ever find him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Why would I ever forget my own brother?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Because I cannot recall the faces of my own kin anymore. If you stay, that black bubbling will take Omar's face from you too.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm stronger than that. Just point me in the right direction.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Strength has nothing to do with it. Days and years bleed together here until you don't know if you arrived yesterday or a lifetime ago.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then tell me how to keep my mind from rotting like yours.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That is a sharp thing to say. But perhaps you are right — if you stay ignorant, the fountain will claim you by nightfall.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I didn't mean to be cruel. I am just running out of time.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Time does not run here, it only circles like a vulture. Your guilt smells like blood to the things in the dark — they will find you before you find him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was my fault Omar fell in. I can't go back without him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The king who holds this place does not give refunds to boys who make mistakes. He gathers what falls to him and keeps it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Let him try. I just need a weapon against the dark.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The watchers in those windows feed on panic. You cannot hide fear here — you must cage it so it does not rule you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You're already taking a risk talking to me. Make it count.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Helping you costs me. Every secret I give invites the oil to take another piece of my memory. I have very little left to lose.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't waste whatever you give me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a way to anchor yourself — something to say when the dark gets too loud. My jaw aches just reaching for it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then reach. I have no one else to ask.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower your voice. The oil bubbles faster when it senses what I am about to do. A window just went dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Say it before more go dark.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: By the time I finish, I may forget who you are entirely. You will remember for both of us.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will. Just give me the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more — harder to give. My hands won't stop shaking.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am still here. Say it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't waste them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when your mind starts slipping. Use the second only when the pale hands reach you — not before. The order matters.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't forget you, old man.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You will, and that is a mercy. Now go. Do not look back at what remains of me.
